Each row reports the location with the highest index for that ply within the selected component. Cap results cover all four caps. At a point load, the station is evaluated on its inboard side. Global peaks are sampled estimates.

Model, assumptions and validation

This is a linear beam and laminate sizing tool. It is not shell finite-element analysis or a flightworthiness assessment. An index below 1 only means the supplied in-plane ply stress allowables have not been reached in this model. Inputs last until the page is reloaded; export results to retain the input configuration and calculations.

What is calculated

  • Classical laminate A, B and D matrices, with plane-stress lamina properties.
  • Symmetric, balanced laminate membrane stiffness. Unsymmetric or extension–shear coupled stacks are rejected.
  • Thin-wall wing-box bending with an elastic centroid and coupled vertical/chordwise curvatures.
  • Single-cell shear flow, shear centre and Bredt–Batho torsional stiffness.
  • Cantilever bending plus shear deflection, twist and first-ply maximum-stress indices.

What you must account for separately

  • Skin/web buckling, local pressure bending and cross-section distortion.
  • Ribs, outer fairings, adhesive, root fittings, cap load transfer and joints.
  • Delamination, through-thickness stresses, damage, fatigue and environmental knockdowns.
  • Large deflections, flutter, divergence and other aeroelastic effects.
  • True shell offsets: input airfoil and box contours are treated as wall midlines; caps are axial booms on those midlines.

Loads and signs

Forces are prescribed, not predicted aerodynamically. Distributed force is the total on one modelled half-wing, even when a full wingspan is entered. Positive force acts upwards. Positive torque and twist raise the trailing edge. Point loads have independent span and chord positions. The multiplier scales all loads, including enabled self-weight. The root is fully clamped. Angle 90° follows the clockwise box-wall direction in the section view.

Key relations

Aᵢⱼ = Σ Q̄ᵢⱼ tₖ   ·   axial wall stiffness = A₁₁ − A₁₂²/A₂₂
GJ = 4A² / ∮(ds/A₆₆)   ·   qtorsion = T / (signed 2A)
Index = max(|σ₁|/X, |σ₂|/Y, |τ₁₂|/S)   ·   proportional reserve = 1 / maximum index

Strength X and Y select their tensile or compressive allowable according to stress sign. The reserve applies only to proportional scaling of the complete current load case. It is not a structural safety factor. Material defaults are illustrative carbon/epoxy values, not a certified material dataset.

Laminate matrices

Verification and references

The calculation uses 160 span intervals plus point-load locations, with 64 panels per skin and 24 per web. The included numerical checks cover isotropic laminate limits, laminate symmetry, rectangular-box stiffness, shear-flow equilibrium, uniform/point-load beam solutions, pure torsion, load scaling and coordinate formats. No experimental wing validation has been performed.

NASA RP-1351: Basic Mechanics of Laminated Composite Plates
Aerospace Structures: Elements of a Thin-walled Bar Theory

All dimensions and loads use SI units. All mass results refer to the modelled wing box only.
